title: Stress-test trajectory-level differential privacy for NRI
question: Can Neural Relational Inference be trained and released with a defensible trajectory-level differential privacy guarantee, and is that problem materially distinct from existing graph-DP and graph-unlearning work?
acceptance_criteria: Specify the privacy object/data unit, raw-data adjacency relation, threat model, mechanism, release surface, privacy guarantee, task objective, and assumptions.
Verify whether one simulation trajectory is both the computational record and a defensible semantic privacy record in NRI-style datasets.
Audit the original NRI implementation for operations that invalidate a standard per-record DP-SGD argument, including cross-record normalization and batch-dependent layers.
Construct a DP-compatible architecture and preprocessing path, with every data-dependent step either public/fixed or included in the privacy accounting.

Survey direct precedent across differentially private graph learning, time-series/trajectory privacy, latent-graph inference, system identification, causal/structure discovery, and relational dynamics.
Separate trajectory-level DP from graph unlearning/certified removal and explain when each threat model is appropriate.
Define the exact proof obligations and implementation tests required before any privacy claim is made.
Reach a source-backed go/no-go decision on whether this is a research contribution rather than a straightforward application of DP-SGD.
